_about: Hand-written, Nov 17, 2026. Why applications get sent back, from the City of Toronto's own pages. 'when' uses the same tags as the roadmap (checker/roadmap.py) plus 'fails', 'approvals', 'missing'. 'source' is 'city' (quoted from a City page) or 'check' (based on this project's results). The City doesn't publish a ranked list of rejection reasons; BuildSafeTO says missing submission items are the most common cause of delay.

warnings.title: Missing the Tree Declaration form
warnings.why: The City says the tree declaration is one of the forms most often left out. It's needed for any project that could damage private or City trees.
warnings.fix: Fill in the Tree Declaration form, even if you think no trees are affected.

warnings.title: Missing the zoning declaration
warnings.why: The City lists the zoning declaration with the tree declaration as the forms most often overlooked.
warnings.fix: Include the zoning information the application asks for (or a Zoning Applicable Law Certificate if you have one).

warnings.title: Something on the checklist is missing
warnings.why: The City says missing submission items are the most common cause of permit delays.
warnings.fix: Go through the roadmap checklist below and tick off every drawing and form before you apply.

warnings.title: No current survey behind the site plan
warnings.why: The site plan has to be based on an up-to-date survey by an Ontario Land Surveyor (Ch. 363-3.5), showing lot lines, setbacks and grades.
warnings.fix: Use a survey that shows the property as it is today. Ask the City if you can use an older one.

warnings.title: Sketches or messy drawing files
warnings.why: Sketches aren't accepted. Drawings must be to scale, fully dimensioned, flattened and combined into one PDF.
warnings.fix: Have a qualified designer (BCIN) or architect prepare the drawings, and send one flattened PDF.

warnings.title: Unsigned forms or no qualified designer
warnings.why: New construction, structural changes and additions need a qualified designer, and every form must be signed.
warnings.fix: Check every form is signed, and include Schedule 1 (designer information).

warnings.title: Using an old application form
warnings.why: Since Feb 16, 2026, applications must use the updated Application for a Permit to Construct or Demolish.
warnings.fix: Download the current form from the City's forms index.

warnings.title: Missing the energy efficiency form (SB-12)
warnings.why: New houses and additions need an Energy Efficiency Design Summary.
warnings.fix: Ask your designer for the prescriptive or performance SB-12 form.

warnings.title: The design doesn't meet zoning yet
warnings.why: This check found rules your design doesn't pass. The City's zoning review would find them too, and the permit can't be issued until they're fixed or a minor variance is approved.
warnings.fix: Use the fix-it suggestions, or get a minor variance before you apply.

warnings.title: Other approvals come first
warnings.why: Your results flag other approvals (like heritage, TRCA or a tree permit). A building permit can't be issued until 'applicable law' approvals are done.
warnings.fix: Start those approvals early: they often take longer than the building permit.

warnings.title: Measurements your drawings must show
warnings.why: Several rules couldn't be checked because measurements are missing. The City's zoning reviewer needs the same numbers on your drawings.
warnings.fix: Answer the open questions here, and make sure every setback and height is dimensioned on the drawings.
